policies.hardware_scope: Manually screened assembled STEPPERONLINE 24/36 V Hall BLDC motors at <= USD 50. Only J1-J3 motor choices vary; J4-J6 use three copies of one fixed motor model. Only the user's three 30:1 reducers on their specified joints.

manual_screening.speed: At 30:1, the current targets need 900 motor rpm for J1-J3 and 1500 rpm for J4-J6. Every selectable motor exceeds these speeds.
manual_screening.priorities: Adequate torque/speed first, then shorter body and lower net mass. Diameter is secondary but its real envelope remains in the model. Preserve useful length/mass tradeoffs.
manual_screening.rated_power: Rated mechanical watts approximately equal rated torque times rated angular speed. Lower rated rpm/watts alone do not establish lower operating consumption, loss or mass. Efficiency maps are unavailable.
manual_screening.voltage: Keep one 36 V BSA62 winding as the mechanical representative of its otherwise equal 24 V package. This does not establish equal electrical losses or prescribe a common supply bus.
manual_screening.wrist: The user requested roughly the 0.066 Nm class, interpreted from the lower-torque/size request. Use three copies of verified 0.063 Nm BSB41. It is a compact sizing candidate, not a claim that the faster motion suite passes.
manual_screening.unknowns: No shipping weight is substituted for net motor mass. Missing rotor inertia, transient motor torque and loss maps stay unpublished; the existing simulation upper-bound policy is recorded separately.
manual_screening.coverage: This is an explicitly reduced study, not a proof that rejected tradeoffs can never be optimal. Original supplier records and prior run snapshots are retained. Enumerate the same shortlisted hardware tuples in each layout; continuous geometry remains a finite optimization.

policies.motor_rating: Published continuous torque from rest through published rated rpm is assumed; no extrapolation above rated speed. No measured stall thermal map.
policies.motor_rotor_inertia: Published rotor inertia remains null if unavailable. Simulation uses the explicit upper bound I <= M_motor * R_envelope^2, treating all motor mass at the envelope radius. This is a conservative bound, not a manufacturer rotor-inertia specification.
policies.motor_mass: Complete assembled motor net mass. Drivers, encoders, wiring and custom shaft adapters are not assigned invented masses.
policies.motor_geometry: Published body length; conservative circular radius encloses round body or square flange diagonal. Front/rear shaft dimensions are retained in source facts; exact reducer-specific shaft insertion/coupling requires mechanical design.
policies.reducer_geometry: Exact manufacturer model-specific drawings. CS-11-2XH-A uses nominal diameter 58 mm bounding flange circle and 32 mm axial envelope; generic 82.5 mm page summary is retained as a discrepancy.
policies.reducer_rating: Published rated output torque at 2000 input rpm; evaluation restricted to <=2000 input rpm. Repeated/momentary peaks are stored, not used to increase continuous capacity.
policies.unpublished_reducer_input_torque: Unknown; output limits enforced, separate input-shaft constraint remains unverified.
policies.transmission: Ideal lossless reducer and 1:1 local input belts, as in the existing optimization protocol. Published efficiency, friction and backdrive data unavailable; no 75% efficiency is silently substituted.
policies.electrical_objective: Pmax is a mechanical rating-limited objective. Voltage/current are retained; electrical current, copper loss and common-bus selection are not optimized. Mixed nominal voltages require suitable supplies/drives.
policies.geometry_and_mass: Approved base edge-frame/mount topology and geometry-derived structural mass/CoM/inertia. L2 fixed 90 mm, J5-to-J6 spacing 110 mm. Belt side rails derive the needed clearance from the actual motor body length, within a 110 mm half-width envelope, rather than an arbitrary 82 mm cap. Physical contact, frame depth and stock-span checks remain enforced. Link lengths compensate to preserve exactly 550 mm reach. Unlimited joints; global self-collision checks off by user request.

reducer_sources.purpose: Strict user-selected 30:1 reducer palette for the 0.5 kg fast-arm study. No substitute models or ratios.

reducers.geometry_envelope_status: Exact model-specific manufacturer drawing visually inspected; nominal dimensions, excluding a custom motor adapter.
reducers.inertia_reference: Shaft side not explicitly established in inspected manufacturer sources; do not reflect it through the ratio.
reducers.source_rating_check: Fresh manufacturer HTML and retained byte-verified current catalog agree on the selected 30:1 torque/speed ratings.
interface_notes: Nominal total axial stack 17.50 mm; another drawing dimension is 15.50 mm, with 11.7 mm internal reference depth.
Drawing annotates central diameter 11H7 and 20 mm internal clearance. A motor shaft adapter/coupler is required; do not assume a direct 8 mm shaft fit.
Drawing calls out eight 3.4 mm through holes on diameter 64 mm pattern and output-side M3 fastener patterns.
Output bearing load/stiffness ratings were not established by these product drawings.
Undimensioned fastener heads are not treated as a newly invented additional case length.

reducers.name: SITO CD-20 30:1 (user-selected; drawing-verified nominal envelope)
reducers.geometry_envelope_status: Exact model-specific manufacturer drawing visually inspected; nominal dimensions, excluding a custom motor adapter.
reducers.inertia_reference: Shaft side not explicitly established in inspected manufacturer sources; do not reflect it through the ratio.
reducers.source_rating_check: Fresh manufacturer HTML and retained byte-verified current catalog agree on the selected 30:1 torque/speed ratings.
interface_notes: 29.70 mm total axial envelope includes the 2.50 mm difference relative to the 27.20 mm main body dimension.
Drawing annotates coaxial bore diameters 16H7, 18H7 and 20H7; input/output roles need assembly/interface review.
An 8 mm motor shaft does not directly fill the larger annotated bores; a reducer-specific hub/coupler is required.

reducers.name: SITO CS-11-2XH-A 30:1 (user-selected; drawing-verified nominal envelope)
reducers.geometry_envelope_status: Exact model-specific manufacturer drawing visually inspected; nominal dimensions, excluding a custom motor adapter.
reducers.inertia_reference: Shaft side not explicitly established in inspected manufacturer sources; do not reflect it through the ratio.
reducers.source_rating_check: Fresh manufacturer HTML and retained byte-verified current catalog agree on the selected 30:1 torque/speed ratings.
interface_notes: Catalog explicitly identifies this exact 2XH-A variant as input hole and output flange; do not substitute the 2XH-B output-shaft variant.
Catalog direction arrows identify input at the left-side diameter 5 mm hole and output at the opposite end of the long body.
Nominal total axial envelope is 32 mm: 2 mm input projection plus 30 mm from square mounting-flange face to the opposite output face.
Fixed flange is a chamfered 43 mm square, with an explicitly annotated diameter 58 mm circumscribed envelope. The cylindrical body diameter is 40.5 mm; diameter 40 mm is another pilot/end feature.
A conservative circular rendering uses radius 29 mm to encompass the flange corners; treating 43 mm square width as a 43 mm circular diameter would underestimate occupied space.

Input bore diameter 5 +0.015/0 mm has 11.60 mm annotated depth and 2-M3 radial fasteners; this is a nominal match to a 5 mm motor shaft, subject to tolerances, usable insertion depth and radial shaft support.
Opposite output-end drawing annotations include diameter 12 +0.02/0 mm and diameter 26 mm.

Product HTML family summary says thickness <=82.5 mm, while manufacturer catalog family summary says <=40 mm. The exact model-specific drawing dimension 32 mm resolves the arm-envelope choice; both inconsistent summaries are retained below.
Do not infer the internal split of stationary and rotating reducer mass from these envelope dimensions; that split is unpublished.

retained_source_discrepancy.specific_drawing_resolution: 43 mm is square flange width, not circular outer envelope; use nominal 58 mm circumscribed flange diameter and 32 mm total axial stack from the exact 2XH-A drawing.

manufacturer_catalog.note: Freshly downloaded catalog is byte-identical to the retained manufacturer catalog; reuse that immutable source copy.

reducer_sources.unknown_fields_policy: Unpublished input torque, efficiency, backdrive torque, rotating-inertia shaft reference and output-bearing load limits stay null. Repeated/momentary peak ratings are not continuous ratings.
reducer_sources.geometry_policy: Use exact model-specific nominal drawing envelopes. Preserve the square CS11 flange corners through a conservative 58 mm circular bound when the existing model requires cylindrical envelopes. Do not silently shrink geometry to make a design fit.
reducer_sources.mass_policy: Use the manufacturer published upper mass bound per entire reducer; moving/stationary mass partition remains unverified. Motor adapters, shaft couplers, encoders and support stock are separate model components.

SO_42BLR43-24-01.reason: 250 g and 43 mm, but the fresh main product page specifies preorder MOQ 30. Not a single-motor purchase candidate; only 12 g lighter and 2 mm longer than BSB41.

SO_42BLS40-24-01.reason: Compact 39.2 mm current body, but net motor mass is absent from checked HTML/PDF. The 300 g shipping weight cannot establish a lighter motor.

SO_42BLS60-24-01.reason: No published net motor mass in the retained source; cannot import shipping mass or make a weight comparison.

SO_42BSA46-24-01.reason: Useful 0.08 Nm step-up alternative: 46 mm, 280 g. Current 0.063 Nm common-wrist preference chooses BSB41, which is 5 mm shorter and 18 g lighter. Reserve is not a claim that its extra torque is useless.

SO_42BSA62-24-01.reason: Same modeled 0.16 Nm, 3000 rpm, 62 mm and 430 g package as the retained 36 V winding. Preserve the electrical variant in research; do not spend duplicate mechanical search evaluations.

SO_42BSA62-36-01.reason: Retain the lighter 0.16 Nm package: 62 mm, 430 g, 3000 rpm, 50 W rated. Useful length/mass tradeoff against the shorter 57 mm models.

SO_42BSA78-24-01.reason: 0.24 Nm is only 0.01 Nm above BLR50, but its 78 mm body is 28.9 mm longer and its 580 g mass is 80 g higher. Manual length/mass tradeoff exclusion, not strict torque dominance.

SO_42BSA78-48-01.reason: 48 V winding is outside the current 24/36 V study; the long/heavy package is also not preferred.

SO_42BSB41-24-01.reason: Fixed common wrist model: 0.063 Nm, 3000 rpm, 20 W rated, 41 mm, verified 262 g, USD 13.90. Fits the existing 110 mm wrist. Fast-load adequacy is still a simulation question.

SO_42BSB61-24-01.reason: 0.125 Nm, 61 mm and 438 g. BSA62 provides 0.16 Nm with less mass and only 1 mm more length; little useful package benefit for this shortlist.

SO_42BSB61-48-01.reason: 48 V winding outside the current study and the BSB61 package is not preferred.

SO_42BSB81-24-01.reason: BLR50 provides more torque (0.23 versus 0.19 Nm), 31.9 mm less length and 116 g less mass at sufficient speed.

SO_42BSB81-48-01.reason: 48 V winding outside the current study and the long/heavy BSB81 package is not preferred.

SO_42BYA43-24-01.reason: Light 200 g motor, but 0.04 Nm gives only 1.2 Nm ideal output at 30:1, below the recalled wrist demand and recorded J5 gravity loads. Not selected as the common J4-J6 model.

SO_42BYA51-24-01.reason: Useful 0.08 Nm step-up option: 51 mm, 260 g. It saves only 2 g versus the chosen BSB41 while adding 10 mm length. Retain in research for a wrist torque upgrade if needed.

SO_42BYA73-24-01.reason: At 0.16 Nm, it saves only 10 g versus BSA62 but adds 11 mm body length. Manual exclusion under the user's axial-length priority; its slimmer diameter remains documented.

SO_57BLR50-24-01.reason: Compact stronger option: 0.23 Nm, 3500 rpm, 49.1 mm, 500 g. More torque, less length and less mass than the 0.19/0.20 Nm alternatives at all required speeds.

SO_57BLR50-36-01.reason: Same 49.1 mm, 500 g package as the 24 V BLR50, but only 0.11 Nm at 4000 rpm. Higher nominal voltage does not make it a stronger or lighter choice.

SO_57BLR70-24-02.reason: Strongest retained motor: 0.47 Nm, 3500 rpm, 74 mm, 650 g. J2 candidate and stronger J1/J3 alternatives. Nominal power is 172 W, not an assumed operating draw.

SO_57BLR70-36-01.reason: BLR50-24 supplies slightly more torque (0.23 versus 0.22 Nm), saves 20 mm length and 150 g; both exceed required speed.

SO_57BLY54-24-01.reason: Retain the short lightweight 0.16 Nm alternative: 53.5 mm, 450 g. It is 20 g lighter than the same-length 3000 rpm BYA54 despite its 4000 rpm/67 W rating; operating efficiency is unknown.

SO_57BSA58-24-01.reason: BLR50 supplies 0.23 versus 0.20 Nm, saves 8.9 mm length and 100 g, and meets all target speeds. Lower nameplate watts are not evidence of lower consumption.

SO_57BSA79-36-01.reason: BLR70 supplies 0.47 versus 0.40 Nm, saves 5 mm length and 280 g, and meets all target speeds.

SO_57BYA54-24-01.reason: Retain the shorter 3000 rpm 0.16 Nm package: 53.5 mm, 470 g, 50 W rated. Compare its 20 g mass penalty with the same-size 4000 rpm BLY54 rather than assuming an efficiency advantage.

SO_57BYA74-36-01.reason: BLR70 supplies more torque (0.47 versus 0.32 Nm) and saves 110 g for only 0.5 mm extra body length. Manual torque/mass tradeoff exclusion.

SO_57BYA94-48-01.reason: 48 V winding outside the current study; not needed for this manually reduced motor palette.
